narrative: Washed ashore, you have only vague recollections of what happened. The past seems unimportant now. Shivering, you watch the bodies float among the debris. No ships can be seen on the horizon.

parameters: There is nothing here but sand and gravel. Or so it may seem. You feel a painful sensation in your left foot, causing you to take a step backwards. Glimmering in the sun, a sharp object is revealed.

At first, you are unable to make sense of it. You pick it up to get a closer look. It’s a large, oval-shaped silver brooch, the kind that people use to fasten their cloaks. Something about the unusual design seems familiar.

A voice echoes in your mind. “It's a stingray.” Sculpted in the center, the exotic sea creature evokes memories of turmoil and suffering. There was a ship, a caravel was approaching. The stingray was emblazoned across the dark sails. Strangely, your memories seem garbled and distant.

label: Put the silver brooch in your pocket

parameters: You hide the silver brooch within the folds of your tattered rags. Tears come to your eyes. You're overwhelmed by feelings of relief, gratitude and confusion. Merely moving the symbol out of sight produced such an intense emotional reaction. How could it be? What could these people possibly have done to you?
You discover footprints in the sand, leading north. It’s late in the afternoon. If there’s another survivor out there, you should find this person before it gets dark.
They are somewhat small and delicate. You arrive at the conclusion that they were made by a person below average height, walking barefoot.

narrative: You roam the barren grasslands, eventually reaching the western shore. Out here, the winds are merciless.
The barren grasslands are quiet. There is no refuge from the cold winds.

parameters: Approaching the rocky shore, you watch the ocean for a while. There are no ships out there. In the far distance, the coastline of another landmass can be discerned along the horizon.
At this point, the emptiness of the western ocean provides you with nothing but boredom. Admittedly, you wonder what lies beyond the shores on the other side.

narrative: The beach is empty. You hear the sounds of crying seagulls and rolling waves.

parameters: A great void lies beyond the mountainous reefs.
They are somewhat small and delicate. You arrive at the conclusion that they were made by a person below average height, walking barefoot.

label: Pick up the rusty old knife

narrative: Something near the water has caught your attention, prompting you to take a quick look. Closer scrutiny reveals a rusty knife. While hardly ideal, it's better than nothing.

label: Take the knife and move on

narrative: Further north, the beach gives way to a flourishing wetland. You discover a lagoon, surrounded by red pines. At this point, there are no more footprints.
The lagoon has a certain quality of sacred tranquility. Reeds whisper in the spring breeze. Deflected by the scattered pines, the harsh winds travel elsewhere.

parameters: The lagoon is encircled by reeds, thick like palisades. You find a conspicuous opening near the shallows.

The lagoon is littered with dead bodies and driftwood. A few crates and barrels are floating around. New arrivals from the shipwrecked caravel, just like you. Time and time again, you tremble at the sight of the stingray, as each container has been marked with the same repulsive symbol.
Far too numerous and bloated beyond recognition, the dead bodies might as well be left undisturbed.
Knee-deep in water, you pry open the floating crates, hoping to discover something useful. After a while, you grow weary. Having found a few things worth keeping, you decide to call it quits.

narrative: Tucked away in lush vegetation, a small shack lies on the outskirts of a deep forest. You discover a fresh set of footprints on a dirt path nearby, leading into the northern forest.
You're standing in front of the abandoned shack near the northern forest. It's quiet out here, for now. A fresh set of footprints are visible on the forest path.
You're standing near the small shack on the outskirts of the northern forest. There is no one else around. A set of footprints are visible on the forest path.
You're standing in front of the abandoned shack. There is no one else here. A set of footprints are visible on a dirt path nearby, leading into the northern forest.

parameters: They match the footprints from the beach, as far as you can tell.

narrative: Something is moving through the reeds on the other side. A wild dog emerges. Growling, it runs towards you across the shallows.
Whimpering, the wild dog collapses. Slowly, the carcass starts to drift into the lagoon.

Someone has been here quite recently. A pile of bloody bandages have been discarded on the worktable in front of you. There's also a hunting knife on the table, along with a pouch of assorted food rations. Facing the northern forest, there's a small window next to a ladder.
This place reeks of mold and ancient dust.

parameters: You catch a glimpse of a strange individual. Dressed in a green cloak and armed with a spear, the young man disappears into the forest.
Like a framed painting, the pine forest is perfectly serene.

narrative: There's a loft up here. Covered by dust and cobwebs, an old book lies next to a moldy mattress.
Aside from the moldy mattress, the loft is empty.
When you open the door, you notice a wild dog lurking outside. It's growling, yet keeps its distance, perhaps anticipating your next move.

label: Ignore the dog and walk away

narrative: Barking incessantly, the animal seems perplexed by your indifference. After a while, it scurries off into the wilderness.
You have slain the wild dog. The animal lies on the ground, bleeding and twitching.

Crossing a bridge over a stream, you realize that you are being watched. Armed with spears, two women observe you from a distance. They are dressed in green cloaks and blue tunics. Shortly after you've spotted them, they swiftly move out of sight.
You walk all the way back to the southern outskirts of the forest. As far as you can tell, there is no one following you.

label: Go back to the old shack

narrative: Seemingly without end, the winding path takes you deep into the forest. The pines are now enveloped by the shimmering light of golden dusk. Smoke is rising from a campfire in the distance.
There's blood all over the place. A wounded man lies on his back near the campfire. He's dressed in a green cloak, just like the other forest-dwellers.

parameters: The camp has been plundered already, it seems. However, you find a small book inside the tent. There's also some leftover meat in a cast iron skillet on the ground near the fireplace.
With numerous cuts and stab wounds across his entire body, it seems unlikely that this person will survive much longer. Nothing short of a miracle would save him.

label: Put him out of his misery

parameters: Hardly a difficult task, unless you're the squeamish type. Rather than delving into the ethics of mercy, you apply the logic of a sharp blade, in the least metaphorical way possible. You watch him die, knowing that the blood from the severed artery will reach the intended location, granting him a reasonably swift demise.
You find a strange key. Made from iron, its angular design is adorned with the number "8". It's unusually heavy.
You grab the small book from the tent.
You grab the leftovers from the cast iron skillet. The meat has been cooked properly, but it seems to be of dubious origin.
Below the green hood, his face is covered by a grotesque wolf mask.

Despite slipping in and out of consciousness, the wounded man struggles to resist. You manage to remove the wolf mask, revealing a skinless face. Apparently, the mask has been stitched and grafted onto the upper half, permanently replacing most of this ill-fated visage. If nothing else, it boggles the mind.

You manage to remove the wolf mask, revealing a skinless face. Apparently, the mask has been stitched and grafted onto the upper half, permanently replacing most of this ill-fated visage. If nothing else, it boggles the mind.

narrative: You are haunted by the feeling that someone might be out there, watching.
Seemingly without end, the winding path takes you deep into the forest. The pines are now enveloped by the shimmering light of golden dusk. Smoke is rising from a campfire in the distance.
The camp is empty. There are still faint traces of blood on the ground.

The bloodstained footprints lead to another path through the forest. Forging ahead, you are faced with increasingly rugged terrain. Forced to constantly walk uphill, you lose yourself on the northern highlands, now obscured by the veil of night.

parameters: Your eyes adjust to the merciful darkness of spring. The full moon provides further assistance. The owls remind you that one is never truly alone in the forest. Despite the fact that you are left with neither path nor footprints to follow, you refuse to give up.

Rising above the others, a dark hill looms in the distance. The tranquility of the forest is disrupted by the ancient clang of war. Echoes of clashing metal ring out from the summit, marking the onset of battle.
Merely a brief eruption of violence, it seems. The echoes fade into silence when you reach your destination.
A trail of dead bodies guides your ascent. Disarmed and mutilated, their pale apparitions are uncanny. Whoever these people were, they share no similarities with the other forest dwellers.

Their faces are concealed by wooden masks, elaborately sculpted to resemble the beaks of ravens. Wearing nothing but loincloths and sandals, their athletic bodies are exposed, yet covered by intricate, matching patterns of feathers, which have been carved into their skin with dark inks.

narrative: You enter a moonlit grove on top of the hill. Exuberant cherry blossoms form a perfect circle around the meadow. The grass is darkened by the entrails of numerous corpses. A woman stands alone in the center, breathing heavily.
The forest is shrouded in darkness.

Without exception, the same raven masks and feather patterns adorn the lifeless bodies on the ground. Slumped forwards with her back turned towards you, the lone woman is doubly armed with sword and spear, using the latter as a crutch.

parameters: Like a wild-eyed whirlwind, the woman rapidly turns around to face you with a hostile demeanor. Despite being drenched in blood from top to bottom, her features are distinct enough. She was one of the prisoners on the ship – of this you are certain.

Scarred and disfigured beyond belief, this young woman is quite short and remarkably lean. She has dark brown eyes and auburn hair, keeping the latter at bay with a crew-cut.  You remember those eyes, wide and forlorn. Among the cages below deck, they shone like beacons of sorrow.
Lowering her weapons, she nods with a bewildered expression. "Yes… I remember now. You came in with the last batch. The name's Rasleen. I'm a nomad from the Phenris Woodlands."

narrative: "Sure, ask away."

parameters: "This is the Isle of Dusk. Some call it the Isle of Godhead. Doesn't matter what you call it, if you ask me. The island is... merely a shadow, drenched in the blood of innocents."
"Cultists, locked in eternal war against the druids. Never speak, feel no pain. Judging by what I've seen, the latter is definitely true. The Apostles of Woe. Hated by everyone."

label: Know anything about the people with green cloaks?

parameters: "Yeah, those are druids. Conservative bunch. Keep to themselves."

label: You seem to be headed north. Why?

parameters: "You've chased after me all this way, huh? Well, I kept going north because I've been following a ship along the coast. Saw it when I woke up on the beach. Still trying to find the damn thing."

"Like I said, I'm a nomad from the Phenris Woodlands." She seems exhausted. "Grew up on Talonbark Ridge. Been enslaved more than once. Mercenary. Weapon master. Martial instructor. Killed more than I can remember. Roamed battlefields since I was a child. Had a son, but he's dead..." She falls silent.

narrative: Rasleen turns away, closing her eyes. Grimacing, she snarls: "get that thing outta my sight!"

parameters: "The stingray…" Rasleen is lost in thought for a while. "I've seen it, when I was a child. But… everything's different now. My memories, they're like pictures in a book. Someone else's book, not mine. I'm outside of… myself. Know what I'm talkin' about?"
"I see. They did something to us, on that ship…" Again, Rasleen is lost in thought. Gazing into your eyes, she speaks emphatically: "Affliction of the mind."

"Back home, it's what the Elder used to say. Some people lose sight of what's real. Prisoners of the imagination, he'd call 'em. That's what it is. The stingray, how it affects us… how we are broken inside. Affliction of the mind."

label: What about medicine? Or some kind of treatment?

parameters: Rasleen shrugs. "Maybe someone can help us. I hope so, but I doubt it."

narrative: Rasleen shrugs. "Fine by me."
Rasleen seems ecstatic. "Yes... Yes! We are siblings, you and I – bound by misfortune, fates intertwined. Let's unmask the stingray and destroy it. Together, we'll make 'em suffer!"

parameters: Smiling, she says: "Fantastic. Just give me a moment, will you? I need to rest before we get going. Stay on guard, for now."

narrative: You patrol the area. Having circled halfway along the edges of the grove, you hear something. Sounds like movement through the undergrowth.
Pale apparitions emerge between the cherry blossoms. It seems like the Apostles of Woe have sent reinforcements.

parameters: The rooks scatter in droves when the invasion begins. Forcing you to retreat, the masked swarm floods the grove from all directions. Rasleen bellows: "By the Great Wolf, we have to fight our way out! Grab a weapon from the pile if you need one!"
A masked cultist is rushing towards you, swinging a hatchet.
Blood gushing from her throat, the masked warrior dies apathetically. Having stepped over the fresh corpse, you manage to catch up with Rasleen. She is locked in battle with three cultists.

Catching the enemy by surprise, you deliver a savage strike to the gut, weakening the masked maceman. Having diverted his attention, you now stand face to face with this brutish cultist on the battleground.
Maneuvering swiftly, you creep up from behind and strike the knife-wielding cultist between the shoulder blades. Wounded, she turns around to face you with two daggers.

Blood, teeth and jaw fragments cascade when the brute falls like a ruinous tower. Simultaneously, Rasleen impales one cultist and decapitates another. The two of you have now breached an opening in the wall of hostile flesh, momentarily allowing you to slip away between the cherry blossoms.

Reduced to a lifeless bag of bones, she is quickly buried underneath the dismembered cultists who follow suit. Having mounted a severed head on her spear, Rasleen makes a run for it. It's now or never.

narrative: It's a big pile of rusty old weapons. Take your pick.
Rasleen is about to clash with several cultists. There's no time to lose.

parameters: As you rush to her aid, your path is intercepted by a masked swordsman.
Impervious to pain, the cultist quietly collapses when the loss of blood has taken its toll.

As you make haste across the battleground, you catch a glimpse of a weak, elderly cultist in the corner of your eye. The old geezer appears to be unarmed, yet his menacing demeanor suggests that he is about to take aim. It boggles the mind.
From what you can tell, he's holding some kind of flask.

Charging ahead, your bravery is rewarded with a sudden explosion, reducing your face to a smoldering heap of ash. The unknown alchemical agent has an acrid fragrance, permeating the brief agony of your last moment in this world.
Having kept an eye on him, you anticipate the incoming projectile. The flask explodes nearby as you tumble forward. Unscathed, you can smell the acrid fragrance of the unknown alchemical agent.
Whatever the nature of his nefarious plans, you were lucky enough to escape. Instead, you cross paths with a lumbering brute. The masked warrior in front of you is armed with a halberd.
The hunchback tries to escape, which only hurts him in the long run, as you manage to graze him a few times during the chase.
The brute crumbles like a pile of bricks. Rasleen has cleared the way ahead. It's time to go.

Another stoic figure spills his entrails on the meadow, in this case marking the conclusion of a long life. Rasleen retreats towards your position, quickly neutralizing a few cultists with a sequence of well-placed spear thrusts. Thus, a path now lies open, if only for the briefest moment.

narrative: Chased by a horde of cultists, you and Rasleen defy death in more ways than one, dashing rapidly down the northern slope. It's all a blur, from which you miraculously emerge with all bones intact.

parameters: Pines are split in half by the impact of bronze spears that rain down from the summit. Clouds of poison dust disperse like bursting puffballs. Splashing water as you run across a stream in the rift valley, your movement is sustained by the rush of adrenaline.

narrative: The silent forest is a dark void. Having lost all sense of direction, both of you collapse from exhaustion, convinced that you have fled to safety. Stargazing below the full moon, you are overwhelmed by a sense of relief, as the owls resume their brief proclamations.
You wake up at dawn. Feeling cold as you watch the cloudless sky, you realize that Rasleen is elsewhere. A loud, constant noise resonates in the distance.

parameters: Horses, chariots and marching infantry – it sounds like an army has been set in motion.
You’re standing on top of a hill. Looking around, you catch a glimpse of the ocean between the pines.
For a brief moment, you gaze across the vast emptiness beyond the northern shore. Here, the forest hill is abundant with fruits and berries, ripe for the picking.

narrative: As the noise grows louder, you catch sight of Rasleen. The nomad is perched behind some bushes, watching the ruckus below.

parameters: Indeed, a long procession of chariots, infantry and mounted cavalry is moving on a narrow ledge overlooking the rift valley. The men and women are all dressed in green cloaks and heavily armed. They seem to be heading south.
"This is our chance. Come on." Keeping her head low, the nomad gets moving.

As you catch up with her, Rasleen explains: "Been trying to figure out where the druids are hiding their ship. They must have mobilized their army somewhere nearby. If we're lucky, that's where we'll find it."

narrative: The troops are crossing a sandstone bridge from the east. The high arches rise above the rift valley.

parameters: On the other side of the bridge, druid infantry emerge from the gateway of a ruinous pylon. Above, standing stones crown the summit, partially obscured by lush foliage.
Keeping a safe distance, you wait quietly until the last warriors have marched by. "Dusk Megalith," Rasleen whispers.

"Heard about it. They say it started as a burial mound and grew from there. But people say all kinds of things," she mutters. "Look." She directs your attention to the standing stones at the top. "Triad Apex of Dusk Megalith. Couple of thousand years old, I reckon."

She nods, impatiently. "That's what they call it." Her eyes dart back and forth. "Listen… war's brewing on the Isle of Dusk. Not a good idea to stick around. If we're gonna steal the ship, this is the perfect time to do it."
"The Triad are three gods... the ones druids worship. So they've got three stones up there. Apex, 'cause it's the highest point on the island... and that's it."
The scarred nomad glares at you. "Pay attention. Focus. Time and place for everything."

narrative: "From here on out, keep your eyes open and mouth shut. Some druids probably stayed behind."
Gaping like an open wound, the ominous gateway beckons. The bridge will take you across the rift valley to the ruins of Dusk Megalith.
The sandstone bridge will take you across the rift valley.

parameters: A connection between two hills, the sandstone bridge is the only way to access the heights of Dusk Megalith. Surrounded by ruins above the elevation of rugged terrain, standing stones rise from the summit.
You glance across the northern ocean to your left. The rift valley is darkened below the high arches. A meandering, shallow stream disappears among the pines to the south.

narrative: A full-scale war has erupted in the forest. The armies of cultists and druids clash on the highland battlegrounds. Venturing further south at this moment would be too risky.
The grove reeks of death. Their descent illuminated by the full moon, a growing parliament of rooks devour the flesh of those who masquerade as ravens.
The night is still young. More rooks arrive to join the great banquet.

parameters: While nomads are adaptive by nature, it's still baffling to see how comfortably Rasleen is able to rest on this meadow of putrid decay. Waving dismissively, she groans: "unless it's urgent, shut your trap."

narrative: You remove the white wooden mask from one of the corpses. There is nothing special about the lifeless face that you have uncovered. Admittedly, the raven mask itself is well crafted.
The two of you cautiously advance towards the ruins on the other side. You notice the embrasures on the wall.

Halfway across the bridge, Rasleen suddenly collapses. Struck down by an arrow, the nomad squirms near the precipice. As you may have feared, there is an archer hiding somewhere behind the fortifications of the ruinous pylon.

parameters: You turn around to escape. Several arrows cripple your legs. Staggering, you become an easy target, eventually falling off the bridge like a confused porcupine. You face death in the rift valley below.
Dismissively, Rasleen growls: "Don't worry about me!"

narrative: You run across the bridge, narrowly avoiding the projectiles. Having entered the ruins of Dusk Megalith, you confront the archer. She pulls out a dagger from her cloak and leaps forward to attack.
The young druid was no match for your martial prowess. Staggering through the entrance, Rasleen approaches. "This is bad, really bad." Coughing, she kneels down to grab the bow.

parameters: "Got hit by a poison-tipped arrow. You gotta find the antidote, or I'm dead, simple as that. I'll stay behind, for now…"
"And find the damned ship too, while you're at it. Good luck." Armed with the bow, she retreats to the fortified position previously occupied by the young archer.

label: Explore the ruins of Dusk Megalith

narrative: Above the sunlit ruins, the standing stones of Triad Apex crown the summit. A parliament of rooks quietly watches from above, crowding the megalithic structure.

parameters: The standing stones are surrounded by wilderness. Barely visible in the tall grass nearby, a clay pot contains several torches.
You grab one of the torches from the clay pot.
You walk among the scattered pines on the summit, failing to discover anything of significance.

narrative: You approach the monumental standing stones. There are three of them, placed around a horizontal slab of red granite. The slab seems just about large enough to make room for a person of average height. Hieroglyphic inscriptions have been carved into the standing stones.

parameters: The hieroglyphs are beautiful, yet incomprehensible.

narrative: Beyond the pines to the east, you discover a mysterious hole in the ground. Looking down, you notice that a massive boulder lies at the bottom of the pit.
There's a strange hole in the ground beyond the pines to the east. A massive boulder lies at the bottom of the pit.

parameters: It won't budge, not even slightly.
By making use of the iron lever, you are able to remove the boulder. Seemingly bottomless, a dark pit is revealed below.

narrative: "MEYM. All-Father Moon the God of Death. A Thousand Rooks on the Black Throne. The Pale God-King of the Underworld."
"PHENRIS. Son of Meym. The Great Wolf, God of War and Justice. The Nomadic Beacon, showing the way from the Black Ashes of Cataclysm."
"NIERVA. Daughter of Meym. The Shapeshifter, Goddess of Fire and Deception. The Corridor of Flame, the Fiery Orb, the Nine Masks. The Arbiter of Cataclysm."
A narrow ledge spirals down along the edges of the dark pit.

parameters: Contracting like a granite funnel, the cavernous vortex extends deep below the earth.

narrative: Having walked through the narrow archway, you discover the antechamber to a hall of crypts.
You have entered the antechamber to a hall of crypts.

parameters: Most of the crypts are sealed shut. However, a few of them can be accessed, their doors crumbled by the ravages of time.
You increase your wealth in the dusty old crypts.

narrative: You discover the hallways of ancient catacombs. It's dark and quiet down here.
It's dark and quiet in the catacombs.

parameters: A plethora of sarcophagi are lined up along the walls. A dark tunnel lies ahead.
There is no discernible way to open these massive stone caskets, with the sole exception of one damaged sarcophagus.
You discover the mummified remains of an ancient druid. Arms crossed, the face is adorned with a white mask.
You remove the death mask from the mummified remains in the broken sarcophagus.
It's a dead end. The ceiling has collapsed. The floor is littered with the bone fragments of previous intruders. It seems like these unfortunate souls have left a few trinkets behind.
Old equipment, most of it useless.

narrative: Downstairs, you discover a hall of doorways. Marked with numerals, stone doors lead to private living quarters.
The hallway is quiet and nebulous. Private living quarters are locked behind every stone door, marked with numerals.

parameters: The hallway is quiet and nebulous. There are ten doors on each side, numbered from one to twenty. The stone doors are locked, without exception. You discover a descending staircase at one end of the hallway. At the other end, you discover a bright passageway.

narrative: Which door would you like to unlock?

parameters: No matter which door you try, it seems that the locking mechanism is too advanced. You would have to acquire more sophisticated tools in order to disable the locks in this corridor.

narrative: You step out on the desolate plateau of a secret harbor. A merchant is loitering nearby. Further down, a druid warship is anchored. Beyond the ship, the northern sea beckons.
Silence reigns over the sunlit walkway of Port Spire. A merchant is loitering nearby. The druid warship is anchored at the far end of the clandestine harbor.

parameters: Facing the ocean to the northeast, Port Spire is tucked away in a mountainous cove.
Three sandstone buildings are lined up along the walkway. There's an old tavern, a fortified tower house and a warehouse.
At the far end of the harbor, wooden scaffoldings envelop the remaining structure of a ruinous lighthouse.
The upper half of the lighthouse has collapsed and is mostly submerged in the water behind the ship.
Aside from the merchant, there doesn't seem to be anyone else around, at least not in plain view.
Glimmering in the sun, the northern sea beckons.

narrative: Downstairs, there is a dark entryway to a prison. The iron gate is closed.

parameters: It doesn't work, no matter how hard you try.

narrative: You approach the gateway to the bridge. Peering through the embrasure, Rasleen guards the entrance with her bow.  "You're back. Any luck?"
Coughing miserably, she replies: "Shame. I'll be here, waiting."
"Great." She coughs. "But I'm not goin' anywhere 'til you find the antidote."
She looks at it, coughing violently. "Seems legit. You better get cooking."

"Indeed. The odds are stacked against us." She coughs. "Let me give you a word of advice... sometimes it's better to avoid conflict, especially in a case like this. Sometimes it's better to blend in... You should keep that in mind."

parameters: "Druids are commonly known as 'green-cloaks'... they don't like it, but it makes sense. Perhaps if you could find such a garment, you'd be able to explore the ruins without attracting unwanted attention. Disguising yourself is an artform, however... and it might require a little bit of finesse. Just a thought..."
Half-choked, the nomad replies: "Be careful... and hurry up. I don't want to be here when the others return from the frontlines..."

narrative: You approach the gateway to the bridge. Peering through the embrasure, Rasleen guards the entrance with her bow. She looks at you and says: “You really shouldn’t be wearing that mask, unless you are trying to attract attention…”

parameters: “The raven mask. Remember those cultists we fought in the grove? They are known as the Apostles of Woe. Druids have been at war with them for thousands of years.”
“This is a druid stronghold. If they see you wearing that mask, you will be attacked on sight.”

narrative: She coughs. “We are intruders here. No need to make matters worse… now, find the antidote, before it’s too late.”

label: I'll try my best. See you later

narrative: “We are intruders here. No need to make matters worse… but, if you’re looking for a fight, then by all means, wear the damned mask…” She coughs. “Just get me the antidote. You better find it soon, or I’m dead…”

label: I'll try my best. See you later

narrative: Ominous and guttural, a deep growl echoes in the catacombs. Mane glistening, a black lion emerges from the shadows. Menacing, the ferocious creature approaches.

parameters: One last roar echoes in the catacombs when the black lion collapses.
There is no escape. The claws of the black lion rip open your chest, leaving you to bleed out on the dusty floor.
There is no escape. With ease, the black lion intercepts your path to the staircase. Roaring, the creature leaps at you. You feel pain when the talons rip your torso.

narrative: When you remove the lid, a cloud of poison dust is released from the sarcophagus.

label: Close your eyes and hold your breath

parameters: You are left unaffected by the poison cloud.
Overwhelmed by the poisonous cloud, you collapse on the floor, coughing and retching. Breathless and blinded by tears of blood, you have no choice but to endure a painful death.
You are unable to resist the adverse effects of the poison cloud, instead forced to endure immeasurable torment.
You swiftly avoid the poison cloud. Now that the dust has been dispersed, it should be safe to approach the sarcophagus.
You're too slow. The poisonous cloud enters your bloodstream, leaving you paralyzed on the dusty floor. You endure a painful death in the darkness of the catacombs.
You're too slow. Coughing violently with tears running down your cheeks, you gradually come to your senses as the poison cloud is dispersed around you.

label: Wait for the cloud to disperse

narrative: You hear the ocean. The passageway is illuminated by sunlight.
You try the key that you took from the wounded man in the forest. The key fits and the stone door is unlocked.
You approach the stone door.
On the other side, you discover a small chamber. There's a simple wooden bed next to a wardrobe and a chest of drawers.
There's a small bedroom on the other side.

parameters: You remove the green cloak from the wardrobe.

label: Look inside the chest of drawers

parameters: You rummage through the chest of drawers.
There's an empty chamber pot and a pair of fur moccasins under the bed. Something is glistening behind the chamber pot.
There's an empty chamber pot and a pair of fur moccasins under the bed.

narrative: You try the key that you took from the assassin. The iron key fits and the stone door is unlocked.
You approach the stone door.
On the other side, you discover a dormitory. There are eight bunk beds, three wardrobes, a couple of chairs and a sturdy iron strongbox.
Inside, there is a dormitory with eight bunk beds, three wardrobes, a couple of chairs and a sturdy iron strongbox.

parameters: You find a green cloak inside the wardrobe.
The wardrobe is empty, aside from a small parchment.
The iron strongbox is locked. You don't have the key.
You grab the cloak from the wardrobe.
The floor is dusty and the chamber pots reek.

label: Pick the lock on the strongbox

parameters: You fail in your attempt to disable the lock.

narrative: You try the key that you found in the old tavern on Port Spire. The key fits and the stone door is unlocked.
You approach the stone door.
On the other side, you discover a small office. The furniture is barely visible in this vast disarray of parchments, books and stone tablets. A broken mirror hangs on the wall.
There's a small office on the other side. It's highly disorganized. A broken mirror hangs on the wall.

You've got him in a tight grip, but time is of the essence.

narrative: Typically, this would be an instance when other, less refined storytellers find a way to insert the expression "tail behind your legs", which seems needlessly judgmental. In any case, you leave the cavern behind - for the time being.

parameters: Infuriated, the guard bellows: "By the Great Wolf, I'm not a beggar! You'll regret this when I break every last bone in your body!" He swings at you.

He pockets the gold. "That should be enough for me to let you live. It's just that... I've grown tired of your face. You should leave before I rip it apart."

parameters: "So tell me, what are you doing here? The war is far from over."
Shaking his head, the guard says: "Enough already. You're an impostor. Prepare to die!"
"Finally. I've been on guard duty for twenty hours straight. Time to get some rest." The prison guard walks away.

narrative: Your cover is blown. The prison guard is marching in your direction.
You hear a voice in the darkness. "Wait."
You're caught off guard by the sudden incision of a rusty blade, splitting your raven mask in half. The wooden fragments drop to the floor, leaving your face exposed.

parameters: A cowled prison guard emerges from the shadows. The druid says: "You have come to the wrong place, cultist. None of your brethren are imprisoned here. You will find their bones in the Chamber of Nemesis."

"Interesting. Cultists never break their vow of silence... which means that you are telling the truth." The prison guard chuckles. "No matter. You are trespassing... and for this reason, I can't allow you to live."

narrative: You find Rasleen in one of the prison cells. She's unconscious on the floor.

parameters: You fail to disable the lock.

narrative: Rasleen wakes up when you enter the prison cell. She seems miserable. "Oh... there you are. The antidote... do you have it?"
Rasleen sits on the floor in her prison cell. Coughing violently, she looks at you and asks: "Do you have the antidote?"
"You better hurry up. I'm not long for this world..."
You hand over the small flask to Rasleen. "By the Great Wolf! I owe you my life." She drinks the antidote. "Listen..."
Rasleen sits on the floor in her prison cell. She seems to have recovered, to some extent. "Any progress?"

parameters: "Stay with me for a while. I'd love to get outta here, but I'm still feelin' weak. Plus, I've been thinking…"
"The stingray." She takes a deep breath. "The stingray has been on my mind ever since I woke up on that damned beach. Even if I wasn't fully aware of it…"

"The affliction of the mind. The stingray is like a parasite, embedded in my skull. When I killed that man in the forest, I saw it. When I killed those cultists on the hill, it kept me going. There was a strange voice in my head…"

"Don't get me wrong. The bloodlust was always in me. Once awakened, it's hard to put it to rest. But this was different… I just kept killing, for no reason. And the voice encouraged me. I should've left the grove, but I didn't."

"That's right, you broke the spell. Or maybe you didn't, I'm not sure. That's the point. Maybe we were meant to come to this island, even if the shipwreck was an accident. Maybe they cursed our minds with this affliction to control us, to get rid of the competition."
"Crime lords. Exiles. Slave masters. Opium barons."
Rasleen starts coughing. "It's a long story. Trust me on this, for now. If I'm right, then I know where we need to go next."
"The Town of Set. From what I hear, the place is crawling with opium smugglers. If nothing else, it's a good place to start. Question is, can we get there?"

"A deserter? Among the druids? I've never heard of such a thing. Times really are changing." Rasleen chuckles. "Well, if you're gonna free the prisoners, then you need to handle the prison guards first."

narrative: Nodding, the scarred nomad says: "I'll be waiting."
Having turned the corner, you approach the next cell block. There are no vacant cells in this corridor.
This is the second cell block in the east wing.

parameters: There are eight cells on each side of the dungeon hallway. The entrances are marked with numerals, ranging from 17 to 32.

label: Go back to the previous cell block

narrative: The scarred nomad stands up. "Let's get moving."

parameters: One by one, you release the prisoners from their cells. Confused, the pale men and women join the growing procession behind you. As you walk down the dungeon hallways, Rasleen makes sure that the prisoners keep quiet.

narrative: Having freed all the prisoners, you head upstairs to the living quarters. Rasleen keeps everyone in line as the procession walks down the corridor.
Rasleen loses control over the crowd. The prisoners swarm the harbor, rushing toward the ship. Ato Triasteen the deserter stands in their way, having drawn his longbow.

parameters: He bellows: "Listen up! No one will be left behind. But you must proceed in an orderly fashion, you hear me?" Begrudgingly, the desperate prisoners comply. Approaching the ship, Rasleen looks over her shoulder and says: "Come on, let's go."

narrative: As you're about to enter the passageway, you hear Rasleen screaming from the ship: "Where are you going? We have to leave now!"
The crowd of impatient prisoners have already taken their places behind the oars. Ato Triasteen the Deserter approaches when you board the ship. "Ready when you are, captain."
There are no signs of life, human or otherwise. You discover an old toolshed near the southern shore.
You walk among the broken structures of neglected farmlands. There's an old toolshed near the southern shore.

parameters: Whatever lies beyond the southern sea is concealed behind mountainous reefs.
You find a shovel. It's leaning against the wall inside the shed.
There is nothing here, aside from the bones of dead rats.
You grab the shovel in the old shed and step outside.

narrative: Many decades of neglect have buried the desolate farmlands underneath a layer of forgetfulness, as if to hide the shameful mark of human presence. Devoured by wilderness, foundations crumble and tools rust, tucked away below moss and lichen.
You grab your shovel and start digging. It's hard work, but after a while you finally unearth a wooden casket, large enough to contain a person of average size.

parameters: You remove the lid, exposing the skeletal remains of a dead human.
The arms have been folded around a rusty metal box, kept close to the chest. Old and brittle, the ribcage has crumbled beneath the mysterious container.
The bones fall apart when you grab the rusty box. You find a bronze mallet and some coins inside.

label: Wipe the sweat from your brow

narrative: There's an old grave behind the shack, marked by a simple wooden board.

parameters: Slightly askew, the wooden grave marker is surrounded by weeds and sunflowers. The inscriptions are no longer legible.

narrative: The grave in front of you has been plundered.
The grave behind the shack has been desecrated. Crumbled bones are exposed to sunlight inside the open casket. The wooden marker stands next to a pile of dirt.

parameters: Slightly askew, the wooden grave marker is surrounded by weeds and sunflowers. The inscriptions are no longer legible.

narrative: The front door has been left slightly ajar. Partially broken, it may have been opened by force.
At the bottom of the pit, you stand in front of a hollow gate. The tall structure is adorned with sculpted hieroglyphs.
You have returned to the hollow gate, threshold between eternal night and the light of day.

parameters: The hieroglyphs are beautiful, yet incomprehensible.
You translate the hieroglyphs. Sculpted on the hollow gate, the inscription reads: "Infernal Boundary".

narrative: Beyond the gateway lies a dark landscape of molten rock.
You light the torch.
A narrow ledge spirals down along the edges of the abyss.
Contracting like a granite funnel, the cavernous vortex extends deep below the earth.

"You heard the captain, let's go!" Pale and malnourished, the former prisoners muster all their strength to set the galley in motion. The oars start moving. A unified roar echoes across the Sea of Twilight as the ship departs from the mountainous cove of Port Spire. Ato Triasteen asks: "What's our destination?"

parameters: "Vua, bang the drum! Yat, steer westward!" Having shouted these orders, the old druid turns back to you and says: "A wise choice, captain."
"Roe Island is a backwater region, perfect for exiles. The fishermen of Set are likely to accept us without asking questions. Besides, it's not too far. The journey will take about three days."
"Your comrade rests in the captain's quarters. She wanted to have a word with you."

A motley crew, if there ever was one. Thirty people have manned the oars. Two formerly imprisoned druids have assumed other roles: Vua the Traitor bangs the drum, while Yat Phenrae the Fool is at the helm. Give or take, a dozen crewmembers are allowed to relax in the shade – for now.

data.name: Journey across the ocean: Captain's Quarters

narrative: The captain's quarters can be found in the back of the ship. Having opened the door, you enter the sparsely furnished cabin.

parameters: There's a table and a chair next to a sturdy bed. Rasleen lies curled up on a bedroll. Wrapped in a blanket, the nomad is shivering.
As you sit down in the chair, Rasleen becomes aware of your presence. Drenched in cold sweat, the nomad struggles to speak: "There you are. You did well, my friend."
"Terrible, to be honest. According to Ato Triasteen, it's likely that I'll never fully recover, because the poison was allowed to linger for too long."
"Don't be. Life goes on. In some way or other, I'll make myself useful."
"Don't blame yourself. I was reckless, as always. The gods punish mortals as they see fit, which is why I never liked 'em to begin with..."

narrative: Coughing, she replies: "Yeah. Suppose I have a confession to make."

parameters: "Where to begin? Knowing that your mind is afflicted, I have to ask… are you familiar with the plight of the nomads?"

"Times are hard for the nomads of Tem Khiris. Our suffering is twofold. The rising city-states devour the ancestral lands of our peoples. The abolition of slavery gave rise to a black market, fed by the slave poachers who hunt our kind, as we remain unprotected by the law."

narrative: She nods. "Do you know about the recent war in the Phenris Woodlands?"

parameters: "My homeland was the last refuge of nomads on the western highlands of Tem Khiris. For more than a century, my people resisted the city-state of Roeburgh. Last year, there was a massive uprising. We struggled to evict the occupying force from the Phenris Woodlands, once and for all."

"We lost." She sighs. "The Roeburgh Militia gave us a choice: exile, conscription or death. Most were exiled to the Deadlands of Triniset. Some chose death and were executed on the spot. A few traitors became soldiers in the Militia."
Rasleen shrugs. "I was already on the run. Their triumphant ritual of humiliation was described to me afterwards."

narrative: "My tribe was always the most militant and independent among the nomads in the Phenris Woodlands. When our lands had been conquered by the city-state of Roeburgh, I had no trouble adapting to life as a fugitive."

parameters: "I was making a living as a mercenary in the Town of Sickle. When I settled a blood feud between rival families, my ruthless efficiency caught the attention of a crime lord named Mantis. He approached me in a tavern, wearing a black cloak…"

"Relax, we have plenty of time on our hands." Rasleen coughs. "As I was saying, the crime lord named Mantis approached me. Attached to his black cloak was a silver brooch, just like the one you found on the beach."
"That's exactly right. At the time, the symbol seemed vaguely ominous. Unable to recall where I had seen it before, I dismissed my suspicions and accepted his job offer."

"It's the unfortunate truth. Much like yours, my mind is afflicted. Unlike you, I've had plenty of time to reflect and put my broken memories back in order. The affliction of the mind is what delayed this confession, nothing else."

"Long story short, I did a few jobs for Mantis. Murder for hire, extortion – that sort of thing. The targets were rival factions in the opium trade. Having done similar work for other smuggling networks in the past, I had no qualms about my employers. Until their true nature was revealed…"

"The business relationship turned sour when I rendezvoused with Mantis on the Arrowhead Peninsula, where his crew had a secret harbor. They were waiting for me, standing in front of a caravel. The Stingray was emblazoned across the purple sails. Mantis invited me to come aboard."

Rasleen nods. "I had gained his trust. Aboard the ship, Mantis showed me the caged prisoners. He revealed some facts about his organization, explaining how slaves and opium were their bread and butter. I was offered to join, on the condition that I round up a few slaves. Naturally, I refused..."

label: And they put you in a cage...

parameters: "That's right. I don't know what they did to us aboard the caravel. Whatever they did, the purpose was to bury their secrets. I have wrestled with the stingray in the realm of thought. I know certain things. These things can now be brought to light..."

"I remember where I first saw the accursed symbol. You see, my tribe roamed the western part of the Phenris Woodlands, a place called Talonbark Ridge. When slavery was abolished, a clan of slave masters built a secret fortress in the region. The Stingray was represented in their coat of arms."

label: What was the name of this clan?

parameters: "We never knew. Besides, this was before my time. As the story goes, their slave poachers were relentless. My people drove them out. As a child, I roamed the secret fortress, where I laid eyes on this heraldic symbol."

label: Was it the same exact symbol?

parameters: "No. The silver brooch depicts one stingray, while the coat of arms had two of them. For my ancestors, it signified the risk of enslavement. For me, it was merely a faint echo of a violent past."

narrative: "Before I was imprisoned aboard the caravel, Mantis revealed the name of his organization: the Khiris Cartel. He also explained that he had business to conduct on Roe Island."

parameters: "Indeed, that's where we're headed. Unless I'm mistaken, the caravel took a detour to drop him off on a beach not far from the Town of Set." Trembling, she adds: "These memories are painful. I need to rest. You should do the same, comrade."

narrative: Exhausted, Rasleen falls asleep without delay. You sit alone in the captain's quarters, pondering what you have learned. It's been a long day.

parameters: Lulled to sleep by the monotonous rhythm of the drum, you dream of people and places from a distant past. When you wake up, the drum has turned silent.
Judging by the loud snores, the nomad remains fast asleep on her bedroll.

narrative: You leave the captain's quarters and step out on deck. The ship is anchored near a moonlit beach. The crew is mostly asleep, collapsed in droves behind the oars. Ato Triasteen the Deserter approaches: "A word, captain?"

parameters: "We have reached the mainland. Three crew members lost their lives as we sailed past the Plains of Godhead. Having spotted us, druid longbowmen launched a hail of arrows from the western shore. The bodies were thrown into the sea. After that, the journey from the Isle of Dusk was uneventful."
"They were pirates. Or sailors. Whichever you prefer. Their names were Cain, Rey and Luther."

"Yes. Like I said, we have reached the mainland of Tem Khiris. Two more days and nights remain before we reach the Town of Set. Unfortunately, we have no provisions. We need food and water. A few have volunteered to form an expedition and gather supplies. There's only one problem…"

"This is Shade Coast, part of the Lord's Peninsula. Unless you belong to the Roeburgh aristocracy, this area is off-limits. Trespassers are killed on sight." Stroking his beard thoughtfully, the old druid gives you a worried look. "What do you think?"

narrative: "Indeed. We'll just have to persevere. Goodnight, captain." Ato walks away to join his fellow druids at the helm. The night is quiet, aside from the gentle whispers of the starlit ocean.

parameters: You return to the captain's quarters and lie down on your bed.

narrative: It takes a while before you fall asleep. You are awakened by the rhythm of the drum.

parameters: Rasleen has yet to wake up. There is no one else in the cabin.

narrative: "Very well." Ato clears his throat. "Next, we must consider our approach. What are your thoughts on this matter?"
"Most of the crew is unarmed and ill-suited for combat. I suppose that you and I could venture forth, accompanied by the barbarian Mastaba, who boasts that he needs no weapons."

The old druid nods. "I'm a seasoned hunter. There's a small forest not far from here, abundant with sweet water and venison. I shall venture forth with two slaves, both of whom I am familiar with: Vargas and Bernard. In the meanwhile, you stay behind and stay vigilant."

parameters: Having gathered the slaves, Ato dives into the ocean and swims ashore. The others follow suit.

A couple of hours pass by. You extend the rope ladder when they return. Soaking wet, the old druid climbs up, followed by one of the slaves. Shivering, Ato explains: "Bernard was impaled by the tusk of a wild boar. Had to leave him behind. His entrails were devoured by wolves."

narrative: The old druid nods in approval. "Most likely the safest bet. There are many orchards which lie unguarded near the banks of Lake Selikro. I shall venture forth with three slaves, all of whom I am familiar with: Ravenna, Gilbert and Sophia. In the meanwhile, you stay behind and stay vigilant."

parameters: Having gathered the slaves, Ato dives into the ocean and swims ashore. The others follow suit.

A couple of hours pass by. You extend the rope ladder when they return. Soaking wet, the old druid climbs up, followed by two of the slaves. Shivering, Ato explains: "Ravenna fled into the night. Her fate is unknown."

narrative: "Yes? Have you reconsidered your approach?"

label: Hunting seems like the wiser choice

narrative: "As you wish, captain." The old druid bellows: "Come here, Mastaba!" Soon enough, the tall barbarian emerges from the shadows.

parameters: The three of you dive into the ocean and swim ashore. Ato Triasteen beckons, whispering: "Follow me."

narrative: The old man guides you from the beach to the top of a hill. From this vantage point, you behold a solitary manor house, illuminated by the full moon. Ato Triasteen the Deserter whispers: "I will cover you. Hurry up. And please, spare the innocent."

With no time to waste, you and Mastaba charge toward the front entrance. Your path is intercepted by a knight guardsman, whose hastily assembled suit of armor leaves him exposed to the arrow from Ato's longbow. The wounded knight roars, unsheathing his longsword.
Bones crack and blood splashes when the knight is struck down by momentous force. Pathetic death rattles gurgle from below.

Having leapt aside to dodge the knight's flurry of slashes, the unarmed barbarian grapples with his opponent, forcing him to the ground. Amazed, you bear witness to a savage beating like no other. As if endowed with iron fists, your ally batters the armored skull until it implodes.

Moving from one chamber to the next, the two of you plunder the manor house indiscriminately. When you ascend the stairs from the pantry, you are faced with the frightened eyes of helpless children and servants. They beg for mercy.

You walk through the atrium without harming the defenseless women and children. While they are left to tremble in fear, your honor is left intact as you depart from the manor house. Ato Triasteen the Deserter waits on top of the hill.

You slaughter the innocent without mercy, staining the walls of the atrium with the blood of women and children. Having eliminated all witnesses, you depart from the manor house. Ato Triasteen the Deserter waits on top of the hill.
On your way back to the beach, you hear the ominous noise of a galloping horse. Judging by the growing intensity of this fateful rhythm, a vengeful rider is stalking you across the barren plains.

parameters: With no place to hide on the open field, Mastaba is impaled by the lance of a mounted knight. Caught by surprise, the barbarian is left to curse his misfortune as he bleeds out. The armored horseman comes charging toward you. Ato Triasteen takes aim as he pulls back the bowstring.

Mumbling a prayer to the god of death, the aged druid launches the arrow, which penetrates the horse’s throat. Left without a steed, the armored rider plunges forward headfirst, tumbling across the grass.

narrative: Mumbling a prayer to the god of death, the aged druid launches the arrow, but the trajectory is too low. The projectile is deflected by the horseman's plate cuirass. Unrelenting, the vengeful rider approaches, taking aim with his lance.

parameters: You stay put, anticipating the horseman's advance until mere fractions of a second remain before impact.
You and Ato run desperately across the plains, yet there is no escape. Skewered by the horseman's lance, the two of you face death simultaneously.
You and Ato run desperately across the plains, yet there is no escape. Skewered by the horseman's lance, the two of you face death simultaneously.

You move aside with the ethereal grace of a specter, crippling the horse’s hind legs with a masterful counterstrike. Spooked, the wounded beast shrieks and throws the armored rider to the ground. Left without a steed, the knight tumbles across the plains.
Too slow. Your ribcage is shattered by the horseman's lance. Death is instantaneous.

You are ill-equipped for such a task. Having shattered your skull, the horseman mounts the broken remains of your severed head on his lance. You observe this moment of triumphant retribution as your soul drifts toward the Underworld.

You are ill-equipped for such a task. Having shattered your skull, the horseman mounts the broken remains of your severed head on his lance. You observe this moment of triumphant retribution as your soul drifts toward the Underworld.
You strike the armored horseman to the ground with a forward thrust. The rusty spike of your bronze halberd fails to breach his plate cuirass. Spooked, the horse disappears into the night.
You strike the armored horseman to the ground with a forward thrust. The bronze javelin fails to breach his plate cuirass. Spooked, the horse disappears into the night.
You strike the armored horseman to the ground with a forward thrust, breaching his plate cuirass with the spike of your bronze halberd. Spooked, the horse disappears into the night.
You strike the armored horseman to the ground with a forward thrust, breaching his plate cuirass with the sharp spike of your bronze halberd. Spooked, the horse disappears into the night.

narrative: You clash with the knight beneath the full moon. A formidable opponent, yet his windpipe is crushed by a savage blow. Clutched by the grip of death, the noble warrior is left to rot in the wilderness.
You return to the beach and swim toward the galley. A rope ladder has been extended from the railing.

parameters: Arisen from the cold sea, you climb the rope ladder and board the ship.

narrative: You step out in the sun. As the drumbeat echoes across the sea, the galley slowly makes its way north along the coast of Lord's Peninsula. You can still discern the Isle of Dusk on the horizon to the east.
The sun is shining as you travel along the coast of Lord's Peninsula. The monotonous rhythm of the drum dictates the movement of the rowers, who groan and sweat behind the oars of the galley.

parameters: Upon closer scrutiny, the crew seems largely miserable and famished. They struggle to keep up with the rhythm of the drum.
Vua the Traitor bangs the drum. Sweat pours down her forehead. Yat Phenrae the fool is at the helm, accompanied by Ato Triasteen the deserter. A few crewmembers are relaxing in the shade.
The crew seems largely miserable and famished. They struggle to keep up with the rhythm of the drum.
A few sips of wine seems to have done the trick. They seem far less miserable now.
Majestic oak-trees rise from the lush hills of Lord's Peninsula. The white marble of distant manor houses glimmer in the sun.
The stone towers of Cape Ram are visible on the northern horizon.
Majestic oak-trees rise from the lush hills of Lord's Peninsula. The white marble of distant manor houses glimmer in the sun.
The stone towers of Cape Ram are visible on the northern horizon.
Majestic oak-trees rise from the lush hills of Lord's Peninsula. The white marble of distant manor houses glimmer in the sun.
The stone towers of Cape Ram are visible on the northern horizon.

narrative: Ato Triasteen the Deserter stands beside the helmsman Yat Phenrae. The old druid has a concerned look on his face. "Good to see you, captain."
Ato Triasteen the Deserter stands beside the helmsman Yat Phenrae. The old druid has a concerned look on his face. "Captain."
You enter the sparsely furnished cabin. Rasleen is still recuperating. The nomad seems half-conscious. She is breathing heavily.
"Five crewmembers have perished from exhaustion. Needless to say, the bodies were thrown overboard."

parameters: Furrowing his brow, the old druid replies: "Gottfried the Heretic, Sten the Slave and three pirates: Roland, Iocasta and Grendel. At this rate, we won't make it far."
"Well, they need food and water. Do you have any supplies at all?"
The old man shakes his head. "That is most unfortunate. Hopefully, a solution will reveal itself. Otherwise, we are doomed. Keep your eyes and ears open, captain."

"Still on the Shade Coast, east of Lord's Peninsula. Roaming the Noble Heights in broad daylight would be ill-advised, to say the least. However, we are getting closer to Cape Ram. Let's hope for the best."

narrative: "Even the slightest morsel would greatly benefit morale."
Ato remains quiet in anticipation.
The old druid watches patiently as you rifle through your belongings in search of food.
The old druid keeps waiting.

parameters: You hand over a dog steak. Ato nods: "Better than nothing, I suppose."
You hand over two dog steaks. Ato nods: "Better than nothing, I suppose."
You hand over a red apple. "Thanks. Like I said, anything helps."
You hand over a few red apples. "Thanks, captain."
You hand over a pear. "Thank you."
You hand over a few pears. "Thanks, captain."

narrative: You hand over three dog steaks. Ato nods: "That should do it, for now. Thank you, captain."
"Don't worry about it, captain. This will suffice, for now."

label: Whatever you say. We'll talk later

narrative: Ato waits quietly as you rummage through your belongings.

parameters: Ato nods in approval. "I'm sure they will be very pleased. Thank you, captain."
You hand over a jug of goat's milk. "Thank you, captain."
You hand over three jugs of goat's milk. "Excellent, captain."
The old druid shakes his head. "Not a good idea, I'm afraid."

narrative: Just as you're about to sit down, you hear someone knocking on the door.

parameters: Adorned with her crown of wildflowers, Mev the young smuggler enters the cabin. She's carrying the cage which contains the poor opium fiend Arvie Graker. "So there's a food shortage, right? Got a solution for ya."
"Cannibalism." She drops the cage on the floor. "Slave can be yours to eat for 300 gold. What do you say?"
"Suit yourself. Price'll be going up, though." Mev picks up the cage and departs. Rasleen comments: "People have accused me of being cold-hearted, but that woman... she's inhuman."

narrative: "Hey..." Rasleen coughs. "Do you have any medicine?"

parameters: You hand over the flask to Rasleen. The nomad takes a sip and smiles: "Nectar of the gods."
You hand over the flask to Rasleen. The nomad takes a sip and smiles: "Nectar of the gods. By the way... can I borrow the prison ledger?"
"Shame". The nomad sighs weakly, curling up under the blanket.
"Just curious about the people on board, that's all."
You hand over the battered old tome to Rasleen. "Thanks, comrade."

narrative: When you wake up the next morning, the ship is already in motion.

parameters: You are in the captain's quarters. Rasleen sits on her bedroll, reading the prison ledger from Dusk Megalith.
The nomad looks up. "It's a shady crowd of people on the ship, that's for sure. A lot of 'em got connections. Probably good that they owe us a favor later on."
The old merchant sits on a chair beside the small table. "Leave me alone, if you don't mind."

narrative: When you wake up the next morning, a mutiny has erupted aboard the galley. The drum is silent, but the sound of violence and bloodshed can be heard from outside.

parameters: You step outside. Famished and rebellious, the former prisoners have slaughtered each other. The galley has been set adrift, leaving you to starve to death on the open sea.

narrative: The sun is shining when you step outside. Fed and content, the rowers toil according to the beat of the drum.

parameters: You have rounded the shores of Cape Ram. In this moment, the ship travels along the west coast of Lord's Peninsula.

narrative: Hours later, the ship has reached the rivers of Selikro Delta.

parameters: A great city lies west on the mainland. Between two rivers, Roe Island can be seen on the northern horizon.

narrative: A few hours remain before the break of dawn. The crewmembers have gathered around you, awakened by the prospect of feeding their empty stomachs and quenching their thirst.
They encircle the bread like vultures. Ato Triasteen stands guard nearby, clutching the grip of his sidearm.
The pale specters extend their wispy arms in the darkness. Their eyes beseech you for sustenance.
You can feel how the tension in the air decreases. Voices of discontent are less prominent now.
The atmosphere aboard the moonlit galley is far less threatening now.

label: Hand out five jugs of water

narrative: The food is distributed among the crowd. They stuff their emaciated faces, soon clamoring for more. Incredulous, one of the pirates ask: "Is that it?"
The food is distributed among the crewmembers. Ato Triasteen keeps them at bay, making sure that everything proceeds in an orderly fashion.

label: There's more where that came from

narrative: Chaos erupts among the thirsty crewmembers. One of the vessels break when two former prisoners exchange blows. Ato Triasteen does his best to contain the situation.
This time, the former prisoners calmly pass the clay jugs around. A murmur of satisfaction can be heard from the crowd.
The water is distributed among the crewmembers, who seem largely content.

parameters: The commotion quiets down for a second. The miserable crewmembers gaze at you in the moonlight.

narrative: The crowd disperses. They retreat to their places behind the oars, hoping to get some rest before the sun rises.
Enraged, the crewmembers shout obscenities and threats. The tension is palpable, if not mutinous.

parameters: With patient and resolute authority, you explain why frugality is a necessity for survival. Begrudgingly, the angry mob quiets down.
They refuse to listen to reason. The angry crowd is menacing. Even if most of them are unarmed and tired, you won't be able to defeat them all at once.
Sometimes, asserting your dominance in a violent manner is the only way to achieve your goals. Easily vanquished, the pirate known as Cornelius lies bleeding in front of you.

label: Tell them to get some rest

parameters: The point has been made. No one else is willing to challenge you. The crew has calmed down.

label: Tell them to get some rest

narrative: The slaves bring forth an assortment of berries and fruits, which are quickly devoured by the hungry crowd. Waterskins are passed around until the last drop is gone. The crowd disperses.

The slaves bring forth dismembered carcasses of venison and wild boar. The raw lumps of meat are skewered by Ato's gladius and roasted by the flame of your torch. You witness a ghastly scene aboard the caravel, as the starving crew feast like pale vultures with scarlet beaks. Bones are picked clean until sunrise.
You return to the captain's quarters and lie down to rest. Rasleen snores audibly on her bedroll nearby.
